title: (OPT) Admit terminating semicolons on authenticated conditional statement routes
body:
Actual3d16 focused qualification contained repeated T312 failures for agent-authored `if cond {continue;} else {0};` within loops. Current #755 behavior is intentional: generic expr; is an immutable discarded initializer and grants no lexical authority. This is an ergonomics/language change proposal, not a claim the fixtures proved old admission.

Support a terminating semicolon for the already admitted bare conditional statement contour when followed by a required next block item. Preserve parser-minted structural StatementIf provenance; postfix/binary continuations and generic discarded initializers remain value boundaries. Preserve existing scalar/Value-only discard checks; no owned/aggregate discard expansion. Conditions, ordinary let/argument/aggregate/return-operand/unsafe/closure/yield boundaries keep T312, outside-loop T313, final-semicolon P106 and unreachable P209 behavior.

Acceptance: independent current no-semicolon controls versus new spelling for break/continue/return, nearest nested loop and For latch, ordinary branch effects, owned children/checked failures/lazy operands, ensures and sticky cleanup/publication order; exact hostile forged-marker/target/boundary controls; canonical source/cache/graph roundtrips; source+HIR structural/depth/work/storage checks and exact-one-short; interpreter/nativeO0/O2/Wasm. Structural verifiers must authenticate the route, never spellings/names. Specs and compiler-checked help language must explicitly own the new admitted form. No benchmark gain before matched live observations.

Implement as a coherent language/compiler/docs batch on wavect/v0-10-0, PR761, isolated/disjoint lanes and minimum owning checks afterward. Do not grant all ExpressionStatement initializers lexical authority.
